spans.s: + पारग वेद- + पारग, adj. sbst. skilled in the Vedas,
+ मातृ वेद- + मातृ, f. source of the Veda, epithet of the Gāyatrī, a vedic prayer.
+ विद् वेद- + विद्, 1. adj. skilled in the Vedas,
. m. a Brāhmaṇa learned in the Vedas.
+ विद् वेद- + विद्, adj. conversant with the Vedas,
वेद-विद्, adj. and sbst. Versed in the Vedas,
+ वृत्त वेद- + वृत्त, n. the doctrine of the Vedas.

वेद, i. e. विद् + अ, m.
 1.
. The generic name for the sacred writings of the Hindus, especially for the four collections called ऋग्वेद, i. e. ऋच्-, यजुर्वेद, i. e. यजुस्-, सामवेद, i. e. सामन्-, and अथर्ववेद, i. e. अथर्वन्-,

(three Vedas, i. e. the three first).
 --Comp.

वेदन, i. e. विद् + अन,
 I. n., and f. ना.
 1. Perception, knowledge conveyed by the senses.
 2.

. The ceremony of holding the ends of a mantle, to be observed by a Śūdra female on her marriage with a man of either of the three first classes.
 II. n. Marrying,

वेदस्, i. e. विद् + अस्,
 I. m. The Vedas collectively.
 II. n. Wealth,

-वेदस् + अ, at the end of a comp. for वेदस्, in सर्व-,
 I. n. All one's property,

.
 II. adj. One who has given all his property at a sacred rite,

वेदाङ्ग, i. e. वेद-अङ्ग, m. A sacred science connected with the Vedas; six sciences come under this denomination, viz. pronunciation, grammar, prosody, explanation of obscure terms, description of religious rites, and astronomy, Vedāntas. in

वेदान्त, i. e. वेद-अन्त, m.
 1. The complete Veda,
. A philosophical system based particularly on the Upaniṣads, Vedāntas. in

, sqq.; 203, 24.
 3. pl. Works concerning this philosophy, Vikr. d. 1.
वेदान्त-ग (vb. गम्), वेदान्तज्ञ वेदान्त-ज्ञ (vb. ज्ञा), and
वेदान्तिन्, i. e. वेदान्त + इन्, m. A follower of the वेदान्त philosophy.

I. and वेदी वेदी̆, f.
 1. Ground prepared for sacrifice, an altar, Śāk. 31, 6;
. A quadrangular spot in the court-yard of a temple or palace, usually furnished with a raised floor or seat, and covered with a roof supported by pillars, Bhāg.

. A bench, ib. 3, 23, 17.
 4. A seal-ring.
 II. वेदि वेदि,
 1. m. A teacher.
 2. f. Sarasvatī.
 --Comp.

वेदि + का, f.
 1. Ground [] prepared for sacrificial ceremonies, a rude altar,

. A quadrangular open shed in the middle of a court-yard, erected for various purposes, and furnished with a seat, Pañc. 129, 17.
 3. A seat,
वेदिजा, i. e. वेदि-ज (vb. जन्), f. Draupadī.

वेदिन्, i. e. विद् and वेद, + इन्,
 I. adj.
 1. Knowing, acquainted with,

. A learned Brāhmaṇa, a teacher.
 III. m. A plant, Cissampelos hexandra.
 --Comp.
